Signal | Signal Description | Function
STO | Strobe signal output for data output | Used to read the data of the total status output (OR) and OUT_DATA0 to OUT_DATA15, based on leading edge synchronization.
OR | Total status output | Used to output the OR result for the judgment value of tool specified in the output settings.
ERROR | Error output | This signal is output while any of system errors occur with the dialog displayed on the screen. For details on typical system errors, see "error messages" (page 9-49). In the "ERROR output settings" (page 8-16) of the global settings, enabling or disabling the error output for the SD card-related errors only can be specified.
RUN | Run mode output | This signal is output while this machine operates in Run mode.
COMOUT1 | Common for terminal block outputs | Output common terminal for terminal block interface (OUT) 1 to 2.
READY | Trigger input permission output | Turns on when trigger input is acceptable.
COMOUT_F | High-speed general- purpose output common terminal | Output common terminal for the terminal block interface (OUT) 3, 4, 6, 7.

Signal | Signal Description | Function
COMIN1 | Common for terminal block inputs | Input common terminal for terminal block interface (IN) 2 to 6.
PLC | PLC command readout request | Used to execute command control via the PLC terminal using the PLC-Link (leading edge synchronization). As the request acceptance may be delayed depending on other process conditions, hold the ONstate for input until the commandcomplete address (bit) on thePLC unit changes to 1 (the command execution is confirmed).
TRG | Trigger input | Starts head image (leading edge synchronization). The input is accepted when the trigger mode shows that READY is ON for the external trigger.
TEST | Trial run input | Used to suspend the status output for trial run or any other reasons. When this signal is input, the result data that have not been output will be deleted. While this signal is on, OR output, STO output, and data output of OUT_DATA0 to 15 is forcibly set to normal state (level synchronization). The data output from the communication port is also canceled and stopped during the input. As soon as the input turns off, the measurement result obtained immediately after that will start being output again.
EXT | Disable trigger input | Used to suspend the occurrence of internal trig gers and the acceptance of external triggers. When the input turns on, READY terminal is forced to be off to stop the acceptance of all triggers (level synchronization).

COMIN1 | Common for terminal block inputs | Input common terminal for terminal block interface (IN) 2 to 6.
PLC | PLC command readout request | Used to execute command control via the PLC terminal using the PLC-Link (leading edge synchronization). As the request acceptance may be delayed depending on other process conditions, hold the ONstate for input until the commandcomplete address (bit) on thePLC unit changes to 1 (the command execution is confirmed).
TRG | Trigger input | Starts head image (leading edge synchronization). The input is accepted when the trigger mode shows that READY is ON for the external trigger.
TEST | Trial run input | Used to suspend the status output for trial run or any other reasons. When this signal is input, the result data that have not been output will be deleted. While this signal is on, OR output, STO output, and data output of OUT_DATA0 to 15 is forcibly set to normal state (level synchronization). The data output from the communication port is also canceled and stopped during the input. As soon as the input turns off, the measurement result obtained immediately after that will start being output again.
EXT | Disable trigger input | Used to suspend the occurrence of internal trig gers and the acceptance of external triggers. When the input turns on, READY terminal is forced to be off to stop the acceptance of all triggers (level synchronization).

When the Capture Mode or LJ-V Series head is used, the number of reference images that can be registered and the range of the reference image numbers varies. For more details, refer to "Precautions When Using a Capture Mode or the LJV Series Head" (Page 1-27).

Using the image strip (Page 1: 19), a desired image from the archived images can also be registered as reference image.

Deleting a registered reference image

On the [Reference Image Registration] screen, select the registered image and left-click , then left-click [OK] on the confirmation message.

Or, right: click the registered image and select [Delete] from the context menu for deletion.

Adjusting reference image position/Changing save format of reference image

On the [Reference Image Registration] screen, the position of the captured image can be adjusted/registered and the save format can be selected.

Adjust Position Custom :

-X Direction : Move the image in the X direction (specified by the number of pixels).

-Y Direction : Move the image in the Y direction (specified by the number of pixels).

-θ Direction : Rotate the image in the θ direction (specified by the angle). -Use Mouse : To adjust the position by dragging the image, put a check.

-Clear : Returns the changed value to 0.

Specify Reference: When the reference is specified, the image can be automatically moved for position adjustment.

Format Select the file format for the reference images.

BMP (default): Saves the images in bitmap format.

JP G: Saves the images in JPE G format.

PNG: Saves the images in PN G format.

The measurement results for the images registered as JPEG files may differ from those for images registered as BMP files or PNG files due to image deterioration caused by the compression.

If the JPEG or PNG file format is selected, it will take longer to save and load the images compared to the BMP files as the compression and expansion processing is required.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
13805 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Timeout error occurred during communication with the FTP server. | Log in to the FTP server was successful, but the deletion process does not complete within the predetermined time. | • Check the connection between the controller and the FTP server. • Make sure the FTP server is operating correctly.
13806 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Failed to delete files on the FTP server. | File deletion could not be completed properly. | • Make sure the user account has write privileges on the FTP server. • Check the connection between the controller and the FTP server. • Make sure the FTP server is operating correctly.
13807 | Backup of settings to VisionDatabase failed. | Unable to communicate with the FTP server. | • Make sure the user account has write privileges on the FTP server. • Check the connection between the controller and the FTP server. • Make sure the FTP server is operating correctly.
13808 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Failed to connect to VisionDataStorage. | (Only when using the dedicated USB cable) Unable to establish a connection with VisionDataStorage. | • Make sure the FTP server on VisionDataStorage is configured and operating correctly. • Make sure the dedicated USBcable is connected to the controller and VisionDataStorage. • Make sure the database software on VisionDataStorage is operating.
13809 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Failed to log in to VisionDataStorage. | (Only when using the dedicated USB cable) Failed to log in to the FTP server on VisionDataStorage. | Make sure the FTP server and database software on VisionDataStorage are operating correctly.
13810 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Timeout error occurred during communication with VisionDataStorage. | (Only when using the dedicated USB cable) While communicating with VisionDataStorage, there is no response from VisionDataStorage even after the specified time has elapsed. | • Check the connection between the controller and VisionDataStorage. • Make sure the FTP server is operating correctly. • Make sure the communication load is not too high. • Make sure the VisionDataStorage is not in a RAID rebuild state.
13811 | Failed to delete images already output to VisionDatabase. Failed to delete files on VisionDataStorage. | (Only when using the dedicated USB cable) File deletion could not be completed properly. | • Check the connection between the controller and VisionDataStorage. • Make sure the file to be deleted is not being accessed from an external source.

Error messages Troubleshooting VisionDatabase

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
13901 | Failed to connect to VisionDataStorage. | The dedicated VisionDataStorage USB cable is not connected. | Correctly connect the controller and the VisionDataStorage with the dedicated USB cable.
 | | Communication cannot be established with VisionDataStorage. | • If the message "VisionDataStorage: Unconnected" is displayed on the controller, wait until the message disappears. • Check whether VisionDataStorage is operating properly on the VisionDataStorage status panel or WebUI.
13902 | Failed to log in to VisionDataStorage. | The VisionDataStorage settings have changed. | Check the VisionDataStorage settings.
13903 | Timeout error occurred during output to VisionDataStorage. | Was able to connect to the VisionDataStorage but the processing does not complete within the specified time. | • Check whether VisionDataStorage is operating properly on the VisionDataStorage status panel or WebUI. • Adjust the timeout settings.
13904 | Failed to output the file to VisionDataStorage. | Was able to connect to the VisionDataStorage but was not able to create the file. | • Check the available disk space on VisionDataStorage. • Correctly connect the controller and the VisionDataStorage with the dedicated USB cable. • Check whether VisionDataStorage is operating properly on the VisionDataStorage status panel or WebUI. • Check that the VisionDataStorage write permissions are set to "everyone".
13905 | The output buffer for VisionDataStorage is full. | The controller output buffer for outputting to the VisionDataStorage is full. | Reduce the amount of data to be output, so that the data for each measurement is output at a slower rate than they are output to VisionDataStorage. Or, extend the time between triggers / processing to allow for data to be output. Note: Results data are not written when the buffer is full.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
14001 | Insufficient processing memory. | Processing memory space available is insufficient. | • The processing memory is consumed in every operation such as measurement/mask region adding, pattern region and subtraction filter setting, and library data setting. • Delete unnecessary region and data or reduce the size of shape and the number of registrations.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
14301 | The controller was booted using an unsupported firmware. Please turn off the power once and then update the firmware. | The controller was started using a non-supported firmware version. | Update to the firmware supporting the controller.
14302 | The file for updating does not support this controller. Please remove the SD Card 2 and check the file for updating. | The controller was started after adding a non-supported version of update file to SD Card 2. | Replace with an update file supporting the controller, and then restart the controller.
14303 | Failed to load the file for updating. | • A problem occurred while trying to access SD Card 2. • The update file is corrupted. • SD Card 2 was inserted during startup. | • Execute [Format] for SD Card 2 (Note that all data on the SD Card 2 will be erased). • Copy the update file to SD Card 2 again. • Start the controller with SD Card 2 containing the update file inserted.
14501 | Could no longer recognize expansion unit *. Please turn off the power temporarily and check the connection of the expansion units. | Failed to communicate with the expansion unit. | • Turn off the controller and check the connection of the expansion unit. • If the problem cannot be resolved, the expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14502 | Failed to initialize the expansion unit. Please turn off the power temporarily and check the connection of the expansion units. | Failed to initialize the expansion unit. | • Turn off the controller and check the connection of the expansion unit. • If the problem cannot be resolved, the expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14503 | The internal temperature of the controller is high. As this may cause a breakdown, please check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The controller is not installed appropriately or the ambient temperature is too high (Example: The ventilation hole is blocked). | • Make sure the controller is installed in the correct direction and location as specified in the manual. • Make sure that the ambient temperature does not exceed the temperature rating. • Consider the use of a fan unit if it is not already being used.
14504 | The internal temperature of the controller has exceeded the prescribed value. Please turn off the power temporarily and check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The controller is not installed appropriately or the ambient temperature is too high (Example: The ventilation hole is blocked). | • Make sure the controller is installed in the correct direction and location as specified in the manual. • Make sure that the ambient temperature does not exceed the temperature rating. • Consider the use of a fan unit if it is not already being used.
14505 | Fan rotation could not be detected. It is possible that the fan unit has broken down. | The fan of the fan unit is not operating. | Replace the fan unit.
14506 | Overcurrent was detected on the connected USB device. Please check the device connected to the USB. | • A device with high current consumption (the standard upper limit is USB2.0: 500mA, USB3.0: 900mA) is connected to the USB host. • The cable is short-circuited. | • Check the power consumption of the connected device. • Make sure the cable is not short-circuited.
14507 | The configuration of the connected expansion units is invalid. Please turn off the power temporarily and check the configuration of the expansion units. | • An expansion unit that cannot be used with the controller is connected. • The number of connected expansion units exceeds the maximum usable number of units. | Check the configuration of the expansion unit.

Specifications 12 Specifications *1 When used over 3 m, KEYENCE recommends removing the polarizing filter.

*2 The focus position can be automatically adjusted at the time of installation. Disabled during operation. The focus position can be registered by program.

*3 The maximum exposure time is 500 ms only when the lighting is set to OFF.

*4 Color type only. *5 Monochrome type only.

*6 Tools can be installed by programs. The number of tools for the detection tools and position adjustment tools combined. For the detection tools, up to 64 tools can be set. For the AI Count and AI OCR tools, up to 16 tools can be set. The number of detection tools in sorting mode is eight. The number of tools set in AI Through Count mode and in the High Speed/Standard mode is two AI Count tools and one Total tool, while the number of tools set in High Accuracy mode is six AI Count tools and two Total tools.

*7 Saves to the sensor's internal memory. The images saved in the sensor can be backed up to the USB memory stick or microSD card connected to the control panel (IV4-CP70) or display expansion unit (IV4-DU10), or to the PC using the PC software (IV-H1SN).

*8 Learn tool only.

*9 Can also be displayed on the control panel (IV4-CP70), display expansion unit (IV4-DU10), or the PC software (IV-H1SN).

*10 Usable on the PC software (IV-H1SN).

*11 Make sure to keep a total of each output with 120 mA or less. Residual voltage is specified at an output current of 20 mA or less. The output current is 2.0 V at 50 mA.

*12 For PoE power supply devices, IEEE802.3at power Class 4 or higher is recommended when using the AI Lighting unit, and IEEE802.3bt power Class 6 or higher is recommended when not using the AI Lighting unit. When using PoE, operation may be restricted due to power limitation.

*13 Conformance Class B, applicable protocol: LLDP and SNMP *14 Conformance Class C, applicable protocol: LLDP, SNMP, and MRP

*15 Use only products recommended by KEYENCE.

*17 The peak current is designed to be smaller if the AI Lighting unit is mounted. The peak current is greater if the AI Lighting unit is not mounted.

*18 If the operating ambient temperature exceeds 40°C that the case temperature does not exceed the rated 75°C by appropriate heat dissipation measures after installation as specified by KEYENCE. For details, refer to the instruction manual.

*19 Except for mounting the dome attachment for (IV3-D10). *20 Except when the polarizing filter (OP-88640/OP-88641/OP-88644/OP-88645) is mounted.

Checking the Workpiece Profile (3D Observation) Vision Tools and Functions Using Height Images Profile Measurement Settings that Can be Used for 3D Observation

You can measure the following profiles for 3D Observation. Height

The head's Z coordinate zero point, or the zero plane's Z coordinate zero point is the reference by which the height (Z coordinate) of an arbitrary point in the profile is measured.

Measure the Reference Height and the Measurement Height from two measurement ranges, and calculate (the values are signed) the level difference by [Measurement Height] [Reference Height].

If either one of the measurement targets is undetectable, the measurement values will be 0.000.

The profile's start point is the reference by which the position (distance from the start point) of an arbitrary point in the profile is measured.

Specify two measurement ranges, and measure the intermediate position (distance from the start point) between the respective measurement results (positions 1 and 2).

Specify two measurement ranges, and measure the distance (width) between the respective measurement results (positions 1 and 2).

Angle from Horizontal

Calculate an approximate line from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the angle (angle intersecting with the X-axis) from the horizontal. If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement value will be 0.000.

Angle Formed by Two Lines

Calculate two approximate lines, for the reference angle and measurement angle, from two measurement ranges, and measure the intersecting angle of the approximate lines. The angle will be measured counterclockwise against the measurement target's approximate line from the approximate line of the reference target.

If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement values will be 0.000.

Radius of Circle

Calculate an approximate circle from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the radius. If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement value will be 0.000.

In addition, even if the center of the approximate circle is outside of the measurement range, the measurement value will be output.

Cross: Section Area

The area of the region demarcated by the profile, measurement range and reference plane (or the zero plane) is measured.

1-Line Cross-Section Area

Calculate an approximate line from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the area of the region demarcated by the approximate line and the profile.

2-Line Cross-Section Area

Specify two measurement ranges and calculate two approximate lines, and measure the area of the region demarcated by those two approximate lines and the profile.

Specify two arbitrary measurement target points on the profile, and measure the distance between the two points.

Measure the length of a perpendicular line which is suspended onto a line that has been calculated from the measurement range which was specified on the profile from an arbitrary point on the profile (the measurement value is a positive number).

Counts the number of measurement targets (edges, inflection points, and distances from the reference line) which have been detected inside the measurement range.

Checking the Workpiece Profile (3D Observation) Vision Tools and Functions Using Height Images Profile Measurement Settings that Can be Used for 3D Observation

You can measure the following profiles for 3D Observation. Height

The head's Z coordinate zero point, or the zero plane's Z coordinate zero point is the reference by which the height (Z coordinate) of an arbitrary point in the profile is measured.

Measure the Reference Height and the Measurement Height from two measurement ranges, and calculate (the values are signed) the level difference by [Measurement Height] [Reference Height].

If either one of the measurement targets is undetectable, the measurement values will be 0.000.

The profile's start point is the reference by which the position (distance from the start point) of an arbitrary point in the profile is measured.

Specify two measurement ranges, and measure the intermediate position (distance from the start point) between the respective measurement results (positions 1 and 2).

Specify two measurement ranges, and measure the distance (width) between the respective measurement results (positions 1 and 2).

Angle from Horizontal

Calculate an approximate line from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the angle (angle intersecting with the X-axis) from the horizontal. If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement value will be 0.000.

Angle Formed by Two Lines

Calculate two approximate lines, for the reference angle and measurement angle, from two measurement ranges, and measure the intersecting angle of the approximate lines. The angle will be measured counterclockwise against the measurement target's approximate line from the approximate line of the reference target.

If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement values will be 0.000.

Radius of Circle

Calculate an approximate circle from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the radius. If all of the data inside the measurement range are invalid pixels, the measurement value will be 0.000.

In addition, even if the center of the approximate circle is outside of the measurement range, the measurement value will be output.

Cross: Section Area

The area of the region demarcated by the profile, measurement range and reference plane (or the zero plane) is measured.

1-Line Cross-Section Area

Calculate an approximate line from the profile inside the measurement range, and measure the area of the region demarcated by the approximate line and the profile.

2-Line Cross-Section Area

Specify two measurement ranges and calculate two approximate lines, and measure the area of the region demarcated by those two approximate lines and the profile.

Specify two arbitrary measurement target points on the profile, and measure the distance between the two points.

Measure the length of a perpendicular line which is suspended onto a line that has been calculated from the measurement range which was specified on the profile from an arbitrary point on the profile (the measurement value is a positive number).

Counts the number of measurement targets (edges, inflection points, and distances from the reference line) which have been detected inside the measurement range.

Defect Detection Measure the area of the region demarcated by the profile and the reference line.

Detection Range (Height Direction) Set the range in the height direction to detect blobs. Point

This setting can only be set when measuring feature values based on the zero plane is chosen in Zero Plane/Subtraction Settings (Page 8-20). This setting cannot be set when measuring the feature value of differences to the registered image.

Specify the height direction range in which to detect for blobs with the direction based on the zero plane.

No Specification: Measures both the parts higher and lower than the zero plane.

Upper Part: Measures the part higher than the zero plane.

Lower Part: Measures the part lower than the zero plane.

If [No Specification] is selected, [Offset From Zero Plane (mm)] and [Limit Range for Height Direction] cannot be set. All clusters of valid pixels within the inspection region will be targets of detecting the feature value of.

Offset From Zero Plane (mm)

Specify the start position of the range in which to detect for blobs as an offset from the zero plane by inputting a numeric value.

If [Upper Part] is selected for [Direction Specification], the range to detect the blob will be the range higher than the input value, and if [Lower Part] is selected, the detection range will be the range lower than the input value (-999.999 to 999.999; default setting: 0.100).

Limit Range for Height Direction

Select the check box and input a value into [Range (mm)] (0.001 to 999.999; default setting: 1.000) to limit the range in which to detect a blob. The area from [Offset From Zero Plane (mm)] to [Range (mm)] will be the detection range in the height direction.

When is selected, the method of processing blobs that exceed the range of the height direction can be specified.

Out: of-Range Processing

-Invalid Pixels : Pixels which exceed the specified range are processed as invalid pixels.

-Boundary Value : Pixels which exceed the specified range are processed by making the boundary value their measured value.

2.Placing Units in a Flowchart Measurement Condition Setting Adding Units to the Flowchart

When a new program is created, the flowchart contains a start unit (Unit ID: U0000), capture unit (U0001) and end unit (U0999). Add necessary units to create a flowchart.

Place a unit that runs some sort of delay (capture, timer end, terminal I/O delay, or variable delay) in between the start unit and end unit in order to elicit a delay every time the flowchart is executed. If the flowchart is executed without a delay, some unintended operations may occur, such as not being able to perform screen operations or not being able to upload or download using the VisionEditor.

Up to 1000 units can be added to a flowchart, including the start and end units. When there are already 1000 units in a flowchart, no more units are able to be added.

Even with 999 units in a flowchart, a branch unit and loop unit cannot be added because they are made up of 2 units.

If the various memories are insufficient, then units cannot be added on even if the unit count is below 999.
